html:
SMTO-UI-0034 — SMTO couldn't read the value you typed

GUID: 609fd63f-55fb-40ee-a2d2-f758d87ed0e3
Slug: ui-json-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • This box expects a value written in a strict format, with brackets, quotation marks and commas in exact places. Something in it didn't follow that format, so your change wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the box showing the error, check that every opening bracket or brace has a matching closing one, names and text are in double quotes ("like this"), and there's no comma after the last item. These are the most common slips that stop SMTO from reading the value.
  2. If you were editing a value in the Parameter Store and it's just plain text, select FREE FORM above the value box, then select Save. Free form stores ordinary text without needing the strict format.
  3. If you can't find the mistake, undo your edit back to the text that was there before, and change one item at a time. Small changes make it easy to see which one breaks the format.

What success looks like

  • The error under the box disappears and your change saves, or shows as saved.

If it still fails

  • If the text looks correct but still won't save, select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the field, to the person who manages SMTO. Remove any passwords or keys from anything you send.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A structured-value editor could not commit the change: JSON.parse failed on the field (Parameter Store value/context fields, workflow execution settings, or a model generation parameter), or the model-parameter change handler caught another exception without structured error detail.

What this means

  • JSON parsing fails in an editor, or the model-parameter edit handler catches another exception without structured error detail and uses this fallback. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • JSON parsing fails in an editor, or the model-parameter edit handler catches another exception without structured error detail and uses this fallback.

How to diagnose it

  • Check JSON syntax first, then inspect safe exception details if valid JSON still fails.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js parseJson(), workflows.js (Execution settings JSON on save) and model_configuration.js (generation parameter change handler, which also maps non-catalog exceptions here) raise ui_json_invalid. Validate the field text as JSON (double-quoted keys and strings, no trailing commas); if valid JSON still fails in a model parameter, check the browser console and the parameter's schema for the underlying exception.
  • Correct malformed JSON; if valid input still fails, preserve safe diagnostics and inspect the editor or service failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended value parses and the field's normal commit succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
